signals.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
signals.content: Harness development plays a crucial role in building capable AI agents. Recent approaches improve harnesses through recursive self-improvement (RSI), but their performance gains often come with higher execution costs. We introduce HarnessPro, a label-free method for evolving harnesses to improve task performance while reducing execution cost. In this setting, candidate harnesses are evaluated using LLM-generated tests without access to ground-truth solutions or official tests. Specialized agents diagnose execution trajectories, plan updates with different performance-cost priorities, and implement them as candidate harnesses. Rather than returning a single harness, HarnessPro uses normalized weighted squared-distance selection to provide cost-focused (lite), balanced (medium), and performance-focused (heavy) harnesses for different deployment budgets. Selected harnesses enter the next iteration, where execution feedback guides further updates. Our experiments cover Terminal-Bench 2, SWE-Bench Pro, and ProgramBench, using GPT-5.5 with Codex and GLM-5.2 with Claude Code. Across these benchmarks using GPT-5.5 with Codex, the heavy mode of HarnessPro achieves an average pass-rate gain of 2.0 percentage points and an average per-task cost reduction of 26.1% relative to RHO. This advantage also holds when using GLM-5.2 with Claude Code. Code is available at https://github.com/pzs19/HarnessPro

signals.brief_en:
Title: HarnessPro – Recursive Harness Self‑Improvement with Pareto Optimization

Harnesses are critical for building capable AI agents. Recent recursive self‑improvement (RSI) methods boost performance but often raise execution cost. HarnessPro is a label‑free framework that evolves harnesses to increase task success while cutting cost. Candidate harnesses are assessed via LLM‑generated tests (no ground‑truth). Specialized agents analyse execution traces, plan updates with distinct performance‑cost priorities, and produce three harness variants: lite (cost‑focused), medium (balanced), and heavy (performance‑focused). Selection uses normalized weighted squared‑distance to match deployment budgets. Iterative feedback refines the harnesses. Experiments on Terminal‑Bench 2, SWE‑Bench Pro, and ProgramBench with GPT‑5.5 + Codex and GLM‑5.2 + Claude Code show that the heavy mode gains +2.0 pp pass‑rate and reduces per‑task cost by 26.1 % versus RHO, with similar gains for the GLM setup. Code: https://github.com/pzs19/HarnessPro
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: HarnessPro – تحسين ذاتي متكرر للهيكل مع تحسين باريتو

تلعب الهياكل دورًا أساسيًا في بناء وكلاء ذكاء اصطناعي قادرين. أساليب التحسين الذاتي المتكرر (RSI) الحديثة تعزز الأداء لكنها غالبًا ما تزيد من تكلفة التنفيذ. يقدم HarnessPro إطارًا خاليًا من العلامات لتطوير الهياكل بحيث يرفع نجاح المهام ويقلل التكلفة. تُقَيَّم الهياكل المرشحة عبر اختبارات تُولِّدها نماذج اللغة الكبيرة دون الحاجة إلى حلول صحيحة أو اختبارات رسمية. تقوم وكلاء متخصصة بتحليل مسارات التنفيذ، وتخطط لتحديثات بأولويات مختلفة بين الأداء والتكلفة، وتنتج ثلاث إصدارات: خفيفة (تركيز على التكلفة)، متوسطة (متوازنة)، وثقيلة (تركيز على الأداء). يُستخدم اختيار يعتمد على المسافة المربعة الموزونة المُطَبَّقة لتناسب ميزانيات النشر. تُستَخدم ملاحظات التنفيذ في دورات متتالية لتحسين الهياكل. أظهرت التجارب على Terminal‑Bench 2 وSWE‑Bench Pro وProgramBench باستخدام GPT‑5.5 + Codex وGLM‑5.2 + Claude Code أن وضع "الثقيل" يحقق زيادة بمقدار 2.0 نقطة مئوية في معدل النجاح وتخفيضًا بنسبة 26.1 % في تكلفة كل مهمة مقارنةً بـ RHO، مع نتائج مماثلة للـ GLM. الشيفرة متاحة على: https://github.com/pzs19/HarnessPro

signals.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
signals.content: Beyond basic tool use and coding skills, effectively incorporating visual references into agentic generation is equally essential for applying AI agents to real-world productivity tasks. We study this crucial capability through webpage development, a practical and readily evaluable setting in which existing benchmarks remain largely idealized: they typically focus on reconstructing visual targets or generating webpages from textual instructions alone, overlooking the more common workflow of developing from visual examples. Specifically, we introduce RefCraft, a benchmark comprising 300 realistic multimodal webpage-development tasks that combine natural-language instructions with screenshots from one to five reference webpages. Agents must selectively interpret and utilize these references while rendering, visually inspecting, and iteratively refining their outputs. We evaluate the resulting open-ended artifacts using independently verifiable keypoints and complementary programmatic and VLM judges. Across nine frontier (M)LLMs, the strongest system achieves an overall score of only 52.12 out of 100, revealing that visual-reference-conditioned agentic generation remains a substantial challenge for current models in practical webpage-development settings.

signals.brief_en: RefCraft benchmark evaluates AI agents' ability to generate webpages using visual references alongside textual instructions. Unlike prior tests that focus on pure text or exact visual reconstruction, RefCraft presents 300 realistic tasks where agents must select, interpret, and iteratively refine up to five reference screenshots while building functional web pages. Evaluation combines verifiable key‑point checks with programmatic and VLM judges. The best of nine frontier (M)LLMs scores 52.12/100, indicating that visual‑reference‑conditioned agentic generation remains a significant challenge for current models in practical web‑development scenarios.
signals.brief_ar: يقيم معيار RefCraft قدرة وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي على إنشاء صفحات ويب باستخدام مراجع بصرية إلى جانب التعليمات النصية. على عكس الاختبارات السابقة التي تركز على النص فقط أو إعادة بناء الصورة بدقة، يقدم RefCraft 300 مهمة واقعية حيث يجب على الوكلاء اختيار وتفسير وتحسين ما يصل إلى خمس لقطات شاشة مرجعية أثناء بناء صفحات ويب وظيفية. يتم التقييم عبر فحوص نقاط رئيسية قابلة للتحقق، بالإضافة إلى حكام برمجيين وحكم نماذج الرؤية اللغوية. أفضل نموذج من بين تسعة نماذج (M)LLM يحقق 52.12 من 100، ما يدل على أن توليد الوكلاء المشروط بالمراجع البصرية لا يزال يمثل تحديًا كبيرًا للنماذج الحالية في سيناريوهات تطوير الويب العملية.

signals.title: ASTOR: Benchmarking and Improving Autoformulation for Soft-Constraint Optimization with a Formal Grammar
signals.content: Real-world decision problems combine two qualitatively different kinds of constraints: requirements that must be satisfied, called hard constraints, and preferences that can be violated, called soft constraints. Because these problems are often posed to decision-makers in natural language, large language models offer a natural tool for assisting with their solution. This has given rise to autoformulation, which focuses on using LLMs to translate natural-language descriptions of decision problems into executable mathematical optimization models. However, this research often neglects soft constraints like those proposed by consumers, managers, and planners, despite the fact that many practical problems require modeling them explicitly. We introduce ASTOR, an inference-time framework that maps a natural-language decision problem to a grammar-guided abstract syntax tree (AST) before deterministically compiling the resulting representation into executable optimization code. We also introduce SoftOR, a unified benchmark of natural language problems which focuses on soft constraint formulations. On SoftOR, ASTOR achieves the best aggregate accuracy among comparable single-request and multi-agent LLM methods while remaining competitive on standard autoformulation benchmarks that include only hard constraints. Code and data are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/astor-softor-iclr-E34C/README.md.
signals.score_reason: academic/research signal; agentic AI relevance; large language model relevance; model capability relevance. Final score: 70. Freshness: source age 1.14d.
signals.brief_en: ASTOR is an inference‑time framework that converts natural‑language decision problems into a grammar‑guided abstract syntax tree, then compiles it into executable optimization code. It explicitly handles soft constraints—preferences that may be violated—addressing a gap in existing autoformulation research which focuses mainly on hard constraints. The accompanying SoftOR benchmark aggregates real‑world NLP problem instances emphasizing soft‑constraint formulation. On SoftOR, ASTOR attains the highest aggregate accuracy among comparable single‑request and multi‑agent LLM approaches, while maintaining competitive performance on traditional autoformulation tasks that involve only hard constraints. Code and data are publicly available.
signals.brief_ar: ASTOR هو إطار عمل يُطبق أثناء الاستدلال يحول مسألة اتخاذ قرار مكتوبة بلغة طبيعية إلى شجرة بنية تجريدية موجهة بقواعد نحوية، ثم يترجمها إلى شفرة تحسين قابلة للتنفيذ. يركز بشكل صريح على القيود الناعمة—التفضيلات التي يمكن خرقها—مُعالجاً الفجوة في أبحاث الصياغة التلقائية التي تقتصر عادةً على القيود الصلبة. يرافقه مجموعة الاختبار SoftOR التي تجمع حالات واقعية من اللغة الطبيعية مع تركيز على صياغة القيود الناعمة. على SoftOR، يحقق ASTOR أعلى دقة تجميعية بين أساليب نماذج اللغة الكبيرة ذات الطلب الواحد أو المتعددة الوكلاء، مع الحفاظ على أداء تنافسي في معايير الصياغة التلقائية التقليدية التي تشمل فقط القيود الصلبة. الشفرة والبيانات متاحة للجمهور.

signals.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
signals.content: Systems that combine several large language models (LLMs) often use one context for many questions. When the context is passed between models as text, the receiving model processes all of its tokens again for every question. Avoiding this cost requires a context representation that is compact, reusable across questions, and readable by a different LLM. Existing compression and latent communication methods each provide only some of these properties. We introduce LatComm, a Latent Communication interface that provides all three by separating encoding from reading: the context is encoded once without the question, and the receiver selects what to read for each question. A frozen context encoder LLM compresses the context into a fixed-size packet and sends it to a different frozen receiver LLM, which reads the packet through cross-attention, with gates computed from its prompt. On 12 multiple-choice question-answering datasets, LatComm improves average accuracy over single-vector baselines by up to 10.2 points. On QuALITY, it reduces the receiver's input by 57x and answers the questions of an article 3x faster.
signals.score_reason: academic/research signal; retrieval/RAG relevance; large language model relevance; model capability relevance. Final score: 49. Freshness: source age 1.14d.
signals.brief_en: LatComm is a latent‑communication interface that lets multiple LLMs share a single compressed context. A frozen encoder LLM compresses the source text into a fixed‑size packet; a frozen receiver LLM reads the packet via cross‑attention, guided by gates derived from its prompt, so the context need not be re‑tokenised for each query. Across 12 multiple‑choice QA benchmarks LatComm raises average accuracy by up to 10.2 points versus single‑vector baselines, and on the QuALITY dataset it cuts the receiver’s input size by 57× and speeds answer generation threefold.
signals.brief_ar: LatComm هو واجهة اتصال كامن تسمح لعدة نماذج لغة كبيرة (LLM) بمشاركة سياق مضغوط مرة واحدة. يقوم نموذج الترميز الثابت بضغط النص الأصلي إلى حزمة ذات حجم ثابت، ثم يقرأ نموذج الاستقبال الثابت هذه الحزمة عبر انتباه متقاطع مع بوابات مستخرجة من موجهه، مما يلغي الحاجة لإعادة ترميز السياق لكل سؤال. على 12 مجموعة اختبار اختيار متعدد، يرفع LatComm الدقة المتوسطة حتى 10.2 نقطة مقارنةً بالأساسيات ذات المتجه الواحد، وعلى مجموعة QuALITY يقلل حجم إدخال المستقبل بنسبة 57× ويسرّع توليد الإجابات بثلاث مرات.
